newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: New Guatemala law to make privatization easier.
newsitem.headline: New Guatemala law to make privatization easier.

text.p: The Guatemalan congress on Wednesday passed a law making it easier for the government to sell off state-owned businesses.

"With this law (privatization) will be easier ... it will be possible to arrange the sale through an international bank as intermediary" congressman Rolando Barrientos of the majority National Advancement Party (PAN) told Reuters.
The law would also make the system more transparent, Barrientos said.
The Purchases and Contracting Law passed with 43 votes in the 80-member congress. Neither Barrientos nor a congressional spokesman could provide the number of votes against.

The government, led by President Alvaro Arzu, also of the centre-right PAN, has been working on sweeping plans to privatise and demonopolize the state-owned telephone and electric companies since the middle of last year.
The government also plans to grant concessions to private companies to manage ports, the international airport and railways.
Congress already has passed laws to open up the telecommunications and electric power markets.
The latest law sets out general rules for open competition in the bidding process and for the involvement of international experts or intermediaries.
The law also creates principles for granting concessions, reserving the state the right to revoke concessions, and sets down procedures for deciding which is the best offer.

Both right-wing and left-wing parties in Congress opposed the law, arguing that the people should have a say in the matter and that the government should seek a national referendum on the privatisation issue.
